title: Janis Joplin's birth chart
metaDescription: Janis Joplin's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 28.8° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 9.9° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 28.8° Capricorn, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mercury. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 9.4° Aquarius, Venus was at 14.2° Aquarius, Mars was at 24.9° Sagittarius. Read together: thought that travels by comparison; attraction that begins as conversation; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Saturn to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.4°. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Uranus trine Neptune at 1.3°, and the Sun trine Uranus at 2.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: the Sun, Saturn, Neptune close a triangle of trines. The closed triangle is the scheme’s picture of flow — and its warning that flow, unspent, stays private. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, two placements stand out. The Moon in Cancer at 9.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 19.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 air, 2 water, 2 fire, 1 earth by element and 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 3 mutable by modality. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.8° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 9.9°.
